items.note: Used any time before around 10:00 A.M.; after that switch to こんにちは (konnichiwa), and in the evening use こんばんは (konbanwa).
A neutral daytime greeting used from about 10:00 A.M. until sundown — earlier use おはようございます (ohayou gozaimasu); after dark switch to こんばんは (konbanwa).
Used once it gets dark, taking over from こんにちは (konnichiwa) as the day's greeting.
A casual 'see you' between friends or peers; for a more formal parting use さようなら (sayounara) or しつれいします (shitsurei shimasu).

A fairly formal, somewhat final-sounding goodbye — less common between close friends or family who expect to meet again soon. Compare the casual じゃ、また (ja, mata) or the workplace おつかれさまでした (otsukaresama deshita).
items.hint: the plain everyday good-bye, not a workplace phrase

items.note: Said on formal occasions when leaving, e.g. a meeting. The identical phrase しつれいします (shitsurei shimasu) is also used when entering someone's room (see that card) — context tells the listener which meaning is meant.

items.target: おさきにしつれいします
items.note: Said by the person leaving work before their colleagues; the colleagues who remain reply with おつかれさまでした (otsukaresama deshita) to the one leaving.
items.scene: said when leaving the office before other people

items.note: Said by colleagues staying behind to a colleague who is leaving the office — the reply to おさきにしつれいします (osaki ni shitsurei shimasu). （でした）(deshita) is the polite past-tense ending: おつかれさまでした (otsukaresama deshita) is the fuller, formal version, while おつかれさま (otsukaresama) alone is the casual short form.
items.scene: said when your colleague leaves the office before you

items.note: Said before eating, even when dining alone, often with hands pressed together; paired with ごちそうさま（でした） (gochisousama (deshita)) said after finishing the meal.

Set phrase spoken after finishing a meal, thanking the preparer or host. （でした）(deshita) is the polite past-tense ending: ごちそうさまでした (gochisousama deshita) is the fuller, formal version, while ごちそうさま (gochisousama) alone is the casual short form.

items.target: ちょっとまってください
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 19: Making a Request: Please Give Her My Regards (explicitly re-taught as a dedicated KEY SENTENCES entry ("Please wait a moment."))
items.note: ちょっと (chotto, 'a little') softens the request; まって is the て-form of まつ (matsu, 'to wait') plus ください (kudasai). ください attaches directly onto a verb's て-form for a fairly direct ask; contrast もういちどおねがいします (mou ichido onegaishimasu), which uses the standalone, slightly softer おねがいします instead.

items.target: もういちどおねがいします
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 2: Possession: Whose Pen Is This? (explicitly re-taught as a dedicated VOCABULARY entry ("One more time, please."))
items.note: もういちど (mou ichido, 'one more time') + おねがいします (onegaishimasu) politely asks for something to be repeated. おねがいします stands alone as a somewhat softer, more general request word than ください (kudasai) in ちょっとまってください (chotto matte kudasai), which attaches directly to a verb's て-form.
